Today's meeting of the National Assembly commenced at 13:20 hrs under the chairmanship of the Right Honourable Chairperson Mr. Narayan Prasad Dahal.
Members, Right Honourable Chairperson: The proceedings of today's meeting of the National Assembly begin. (13:20 hrs)
Members, names have been received to speak during Zero Hour. I have allocated 1 minute each for speaking in Zero Hour. First, Honourable Member Krishna Bahadur Rokaya.
Honourable Mr. Krishna Bahadur Rokaya (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, information is being received that within a few hours of the Nepal Oil Corporation reducing the price of petroleum products, some petrol pumps in many parts of the country have stopped selling petrol and diesel. I want to ask why the public, who bear the burden when prices rise, do not get relief when prices fall? The government should immediately investigate those creating artificial scarcity and take strict action according to the law, and also immediately review the fares for public transport and air travel as the prices of petroleum products have already decreased. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson, Sir, the monsoon has already begun across the country. Learning from past flood, landslide, and disaster incidents, I want to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal through the Honourable Chairperson to the importance of preparedness for disaster management, monitoring of risk zones, and special attention to citizen safety. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Padam Bahadur Pariyar.
(13:21 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Padam Bahadur Pariyar (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, Nepal is among the countries with the highest number of accidents in the world. More than 24,000 lives have been lost due to road accidents in the last decade. In the last five years alone, 2,661 pedestrians have died, and from last Shrawan to Jestha, 429 people have died in road accidents. Honourable Chairperson, Sir, through the Bill to Amend and Consolidate the Transport and Vehicle Act, the government is planning to impose a fine of Rs 500 on pedestrians for walking outside of zebra crossings. It is not justifiable for the government to impose such a fine on pedestrians without providing zebra crossings, traffic lights, and footpaths. Therefore, when amending the Transport and Vehicle Act, the government's malicious intention to collect more taxes from poor Nepalis and meet revenue targets is not justifiable. (Time expired.)
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bishnu Kumari Sapkota.
(13:22 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Bishnu Kumari Sapkota (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, Nepali citizens working in Dubai for foreign employment are serving prison sentences due to various circumstances. Among them, 111 Nepali citizens have been released due to the amnesty granted by the Dubai government, which has brought happiness. I want to thank the Dubai government.
Similarly, 187 Nepali citizens recruited into the Russian army have lost their lives in the Ukraine war, and 96 are still missing. I want to draw the attention of the government through the Honourable Chairperson to bring out the truth through diplomatic initiatives and arrange relief for the families of the deceased and missing. Thank you. Jai Nepal.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bishnu Devi Pudasaini.
(13:23 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Bishnu Devi Pudasaini (Nepali Congress): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, the very origin of the state is for the security of people's lives and property. The government is also the guardian of the poor, landless, and homeless. But why is the government being so indifferent towards the landless? Although the government says it has the strength of the people, I want to ask the government: did the people send them to power to evict the poor, destitute, and landless? If not, why is it ignoring the plight of the landless? In this rainy season, when homeowners are ensuring their safety, the landless are being evicted even from their current locations. Therefore, I want to ask the government: is this what freedom means? Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma.
(13:24 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Bishnu Bahadur Bishwakarma (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, news of billions of rupees worth of vehicles being burnt and turned to ash, and then billions of rupees worth of new vehicles being purchased, has created a sensation. Today, the landless are starving. People are suffering from a lack of paracetamol. They are falling ill due to lack of shelter. Without looking at this situation, vehicles are being purchased for their own comfort and entertainment. This is a tragedy. Our new government's new policy is that Gen Z ministers and MPs should also be Gen Z. We should buy bicycles now. Ride bicycles to and fro. Rather, let the construction of Singha Durbar also be done through this labor, funded by donations. I want to tell our government this. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari.
(13:24 hrs)
Honourable Mr. Shrikrishna Prasad Adhikari (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, in Nuwakot, Suryagadhi Rural Municipality, Ward No. 1, Lachyang, landslides have occurred in Kaulle and Semra, displacing 30 houses, and hundreds of houses are at risk due to land subsidence and landslides. The risk of these landslides was brought to the attention of the authorities repeatedly by the then people's representatives 5-6 years ago, and the municipality and district coordination also followed up, but the permanent management of the landslide-affected people has not yet been done. If a proper technical study of the landslide-affected area and disaster preparedness is not managed, there is a risk of great loss of life and property.
I want to draw the attention of the Government of Nepal through the Honourable Chairperson to make permanent alternative arrangements for the people affected by the landslide. Thank you.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Member Savitri Mall.
(13:26 hrs)
Honourable Ms. Savitri Mall (Communist Party of Nepal): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, the people of Susta in Nawalparasi district have been campaigning for 'Save Susta'. I want to draw the attention of the government to immediately address their legitimate demands. Concrete diplomatic initiatives should be taken to stop Indian encroachment and strengthen border security. Citizenship should be provided to the stateless residents of Susta. Land deeds for the land they have been cultivating should be distributed. I strongly demand from the government with a clear majority to address the national issues related to the border and the legitimate demands of the victims as soon as possible. The statement made by the Honourable Prime Minister on June 4, which implied that Nepal has also encroached upon Indian territory, has made the situation even more difficult for the residents of Susta. Thank you. Namaste.
Honourable Chairperson: Honourable Members, the order of speaking in Zero Hour ends here. (13:28 hrs)
Honourable Members, discussions on various ministry-wise headings of the "Appropriation Bill, 2083" will commence. Under this, discussions will be held collectively today on the appropriation headings related to the Ministry of Youth, Labour and Employment; Ministry of Information and Communications; Ministry of Culture, Tourism and Civil Aviation; Ministry of Education and Sports; Ministry of Health and Population; Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives, and Poverty Alleviation; Ministry of Women, Children, and Senior Citizens; Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation; and Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs. I would like to inform you that this will be done.
Honourable Members, in accordance with Rule 136 of the National Assembly Rules, 2075, a proposal for expenditure reduction has been received from Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota regarding the appropriation heading related to the Ministry of Health and Population.
Honourable Members, I now provide the floor to Honourable Member Samjhana Devkota, the proposer of the expenditure reduction proposal, to present her proposal and participate in the discussion on the appropriation headings determined for today. Time: 8 minutes.
Honourable Ms. Samjhana Devkota (Communist Party of Nepal, UML): Honourable Chairperson, Sir, I have submitted some of my opinions to the Parliament Secretariat for amendments to the Ministry of Health and Population and the allocated budget. Accordingly, I seek permission to present my views on the budget and programs allocated to the Ministry of Health and Population. The national budget is 21 Kharba, 24 Arba, 34 Crore, 44 Lakh. Out of this, a total budget of 97 Arba, 37 Crore, 73 Lakh has been allocated to the Ministry of Health and Population, which is 4.44 percent of the budget. The budget for programs and projects to be operated by the federal government is 44 Arba, 92 Crore, 26 Lakh, approximately 58.02 percent. The budget for programs and projects to be operated by the provinces is 5 Arba, 62 Crore, 51 Lakh, approximately 5.484 percent. The budget for programs and projects to be operated by local levels is 34 Arba, 82 Crore, 96 Lakh, approximately 36.14 percent. In the budget speech for the fiscal year 2083/084, the Honourable Finance Minister stated in this assembly that a budget of 101 Arba, 95 Crore has been allocated. I am not an economics expert, but I want to be clear because the same amount is not found in the ministry's actual budget book. I also want to present my views on the allocated budget accordingly. Honourable Chairperson, Sir, I have presented my views on the government's policies, programs, and budget. I have welcomed the positive aspects of the policy, program, and budget statement for the fiscal year 2083/084 that I previously submitted to the government, and I have also submitted opinions for reconsideration on the weaknesses and overlooked issues in the budget. On that basis, I want to present my analytical opinion based on the program and heading-wise allocated budget book of the Ministry of Health and Population, which is mentioned in this book. The Constitution of Nepal has established health as a fundamental right of citizens. It is the state's responsibility to ensure access to free basic health services, provide emergency health services, and guarantee safe motherhood and reproductive health services for all Nepalis. The state must play a role in bringing health services to the doorstep of the people. To provide quality health services through a accountable and responsible health system for the public's accessible access to health, the policies and programs for fiscal year 2083/084 and the programs of the Ministry of Health and Population and the allocated budget play an important role in achieving the goals of the 16th plan. Only a healthy human community can be the real human resource of the nation. If the state has an unhealthy human community, it can only become a burdensome and expensive human population for the state. The budget statement has committed to revising the package of basic health services based on the changing nature and burden of diseases and cost-effectiveness, including various citizen treatments, the Ama Suraksha program, free medicines, and other health social security programs, to ensure access to and consumption of quality basic health services for all citizens. I want to ask further questions about the government's allocated budget.

The budget has been allocated only for current expenditure for central and provincial hospitals under the state. A budget of approximately 79.97 percent, amounting to 44 billion, 72 crore, 17 lakh, has been allocated for current expenditure. For the health sector improvement program, integrated health infrastructure development program, and health management program, a budget of 11 billion, 20 crore, 9 lakh has been allocated, while more than half of the programs have been placed in P2. This indicates a lack of clarity in the construction of ongoing projects and the initiation of new programs. It is necessary to complete the construction of 336 basic hospitals, which are under construction as part of the 'One Local Level, One Hospital' campaign, as soon as possible. Since these hospitals are the basis of health for the general public in rural settlements, their infrastructure development and operation are extremely necessary. Additional budget should be managed for this and completed in the upcoming fiscal year. This can provide services such as maternal safety, elderly citizen safety, and newborn infant safety. It can also prevent the spread of diseases from villages and settlements and provide citizens with access to health services, making the villages beautiful. I would like to request that programs and additional budget be managed to increase domestic medicine production by providing necessary managerial support to Nepal Drug Limited and Singha Durbar Vaidyakhana. This would also encourage Ayurvedic health. It is stated that a National Health Accreditation Authority should be established for the quality measurement, certification, and accreditation of health institutions and services, but the program is not really visible. Currently, the number of children with neurodevelopmental conditions such as autism and ADHD (Attention-Deficit) is increasing. These are conditions where children have difficulty concentrating, are easily distracted, are hyperactive or impulsive, and react too quickly to tasks. Keeping in mind this increasing risk, it is necessary to develop an action plan for its research and control and allocate a budget for it. Mental health is as important for the human community as physical health. When a person's mental health is not good, their physical health is also not effective. The government must arrange special programs and budgets to control the increasing mental problems, depression, murder, suicide, and other dreadful incidents among people. The service of a psychotherapist should be made available in every hospital and health center to provide mental health services to the general public. I would like to suggest to the government, through you, Mr. Chairman, that an appropriate portion of the total health budget be allocated to mental health. Therefore, I would like to request the government. I do not find much budget allocated to food hygiene in the budget statement presented by the government. The trade of food and pesticide-containing medicines in the market is seriously affecting our physical health. Food security is a fundamental right of citizens. For this, I want to draw the government's attention to food hygiene. I am not standing here to oppose the government's policies, programs, and budget. I am standing here to speak on the most important issue of public health. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable members, I will provide time sequentially for the honorable members who wish to participate in the discussion on the budget allocation titles for the ministries determined for today. This has been received based on the order of priority. Now, I will provide time to Honorable Member Bishnu Devi Pudasaini, time 5 minutes. Following this, Honorable Member Jayanti Devi Rai. Honorable Shri Bishnu Devi Pudasaini (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, Sir, I am going to talk about some matters related to the Ministry of Culture, Tourism, and Civil Aviation, and if time permits, I will also touch upon the Ministry of Women. I am going to share some of my thoughts on this. First of all, I am a person who uses somewhat mild language. However, if something is missed somewhere, I feel like speaking out. Therefore, regarding the budget missed by this ministry, I felt that Kathmandu is where most of the guests come to Nepal. No ministry has touched upon Kathmandu, nor has it been seen. Moreover, I felt that no ministry has paid attention or thought about making Kathmandu beautiful. The honorable minister seems to have some knowledge about the community, but he did not mention Kathmandu's rivers and drains, nor did he mention the name of the deity, Lord Pashupatinath. Therefore, I feel a bit disheartened because millions of people from all over the world come to Lord Pashupatinath to worship. I could not find any mention of the Bagmati river, which flows east of the Pashupatinath temple, or its condition. Seeing the condition of the Bagmati, it is truly pathetic. The fact that sewage is mixed in it, and no ministry has addressed this, makes me feel a bit empty. However, I would also like to thank the honorable minister for one thing. He has touched upon Gokarneshwor Municipality Ward No. 1, Gokarna Palace, and has allocated some amount. For that, I would like to thank him. I also feel that the minister must have understood this well and allocated this amount after much consideration. I have a few more things to say about this palace area. We have all just started drinking Melamchi's water. We all know that earlier we used to drink water brought from Sundarijal. The pond at Sundarijal and that palace were built during the Rana regime by the Ranas. The scouts are currently working there. This is an extremely important place. For example, it takes about an hour to walk uphill to reach Sundarijal. There are vast green forests on both sides. The Bagmati flows here. It is a very beautiful and extremely important place. After walking a little further up, about an hour, you reach Thulo, and after a short walk, you reach this palace. A little below the palace is a large drinking water pond. Therefore, this is an extremely important place, and many people go further up from this route. This is also the route to Helambu. Since this is a very important place in terms of tourism, I would like to request all the honorable ministers, who are present today, to please show some affection towards Sundarijal, as it is truly an important place for tourism. I am also going to say a few things to the honorable Minister for Women and Children. Are there no street children in Kathmandu? There were street children in the Kathmandu Valley. It seems your attention did not go there either. Another thing is that you have proposed to build day care centers in 50 locations for the elderly. In which locations are these? It was not clearly specified, so we were a bit confused as we could not understand where and what. Also, it is mentioned that a building will be constructed for the Mangala and Sana Rehabilitation Center. Where is that? When will it be built? For whom is it? If it is built in the name of the ministers, then that should also be known. Now, it is mentioned as Mangala and Sana here, but where will this building be built? When will it be built? For whom will it be built? This matter is not clear, so I request that this matter be clarified. Please do not delay so much, all the ministers, as Kathmandu is a place where you all live. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable member, your time is up. I bid farewell, thank you. May everyone be victorious, Jai Nepal. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Jayanti Devi Rai, time 9 minutes. Following this, Honorable Member Sonam Geljen Sherpa. Honorable Shri Jayanti Devi Rai (Nepal Communist Party): Honorable Chairperson, Sir, I do not have much enthusiasm to speak on this allocated budget. Because we have raised many issues in the policies, programs, principles, and priorities, and everyone has spoken, but we have not seen how much our concerns have been addressed. Looking at the budget, the commitment of the government was to manage the landless squatters by today, Ashar 15th. But now you have extended it by one week. Looking at your budget, it is not even one percent. With 0.70 percent, how will you solve the squatter problem? At this time, the data and the data of the protesting squatters are different. 38,086 people have been displaced today. Millions of squatters are still missing. Honorable Chairperson, Sir, today squatters do not want money, they want land. They do not want temporary settlements in holding centers or any other place. They want permanent settlement. Therefore, until when will you manage them? Will your budget be sufficient for that? Where will you bring it from? Therefore, the government's situation is not visible at this time, and the problem of squatters is not being solved. It can be said that this government was born out of destruction, it enjoys destruction more than development, and it enjoys tears more than laughter and happiness. We probably won't get much to say to such a government. Similarly, when it comes to education, all the honorable ministers are educated. They are knowledgeable, have studied abroad, and have a lot of foreign experience, and the current ministers in the government have been selected from among them. However, you have copied many things from abroad. In education, if you copy this budget as well, how much will it cost? The budget for teachers, which is the basic need here. You have reduced the budget for education. Compared to last year, you have reduced it by 2 percent. Will this make the current education policy successful? You have said that you will create a digital age. For that, shouldn't the budget be allocated for remote areas and community schools? And shouldn't it be allocated for subject-specific positions? Shouldn't subjects like science, math, public education, and English be made into positions? Today, every subject should be made professional and productive, employment-oriented. When will this education policy, which produces two types of citizens, end? Therefore, this is a major mistake, please correct it. Similarly, women and children, there are many issues here. Children, women, the elderly, disabled, sexual minorities, and all minorities are covered here. All marginalized communities and backward classes are also included here. I am happy. Today, the Ministry of Women has allocated 4 percent more budget than yesterday. For that, I want to thank you. After many years, there has been a slight change this year. However, to be honest, this is a ministry linked to social justice. Many things happen from here, and even with the budget, it has not reached here. If we can do more than half of the work here, we can bring about a lot of transformation. Many can get their rights. Therefore, I would like to request that this be looked into a little more. Today, there are more than 37,000 women teachers. They all teach at the lowest level, early childhood development, which is also called ECD. I have raised this repeatedly, and they work hard from 9 AM to 4/5 PM.

To wipe children's noses, to wipe their feces, but they are given a minimum of ten to fifteen thousand, and even that is not uniform. That too is done according to the intentions of each local level. It cannot be considered a permanent cadre, but it should be maintained with uniformity at a minimum salary. This is not what I am saying now. The next thing is that you will accommodate the youth, right? We will accommodate ourselves in this country. We will not go abroad. How much is your budget to accommodate them? Your budget is not even 1 percent. Where will you accommodate them? From involving them in industries and businesses to making them professional, there is no budget for stopping them from fleeing abroad. Therefore, more attention should be paid to this matter. Because this is a government established by the strength of the youth, established by the strength of the youth. The next thing is that I am happy. The university bears 80 percent of the load, but you have reduced the budget by 40 percent, why? And the next thing is that I wish that you will always remain in the present, I also wish you well. Former MPs today, not just in this country, but internationally, there was a provision to give at least one room to former MPs. And today, former MPs have played a very important role, whether it is about constitution-making or its implementation. But today you have also cut the budget of 5 million rupees given to them. You have given 1.5 million. Therefore, I want to draw the serious attention of the minister of the government. Please rethink that, and provide that budget to them again through the same process as they were receiving it, without cutting it. Yesterday, they had a gathering, there are widespread complaints, and today you will hear this. Now, the next thing is that tourism is also what greatly helps the economy of this country, the issue of promoting tourism. But today, for promoting tourism, there are very important places in the remote areas of far-off countries. But you have not addressed them. And I had also included a plan there. It is historically important and has been included in the national list, but there is no time to speak about it now. But you have not even looked at it. Therefore, today, all these problems remain as they are, and we did not expect this from anyone. If you look at women, there are problems in the Terai, in the Far-West, in Karnali. We have reached many places. But today, no one cares about those places, and there are safe houses, but today they do not have the status to get shelter there, nor do their children. Today, by 2030, perhaps the government's policy is to achieve basic education, it falls under sustainable development. But where will those children study today? How will they acquire their basic education? It is very dire. Therefore, the government's attention should also be drawn to this, and the government needs to understand the country, its environment, its people, and its problems in a detailed manner. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Sonam Geljen Sherpa, time 5 minutes. (1:54 PM) After this, Honorable Member Kiran Babu Shrestha. Honorable Mr. Sonam Geljen Sherpa (Nepal Communist Party, UML): Honorable Chairperson, (1:54 PM) In the course of the discussion, I also want to raise a few points. Especially, I want to raise a few points related to the tourism sector. I looked at the red book, I didn't read the budget, I didn't feel sad. I didn't feel sad because the perspective from which Singha Durbar always looks is a bit limited. I compare the Himalayas and Singha Durbar. We live in the Himalayas. When viewed from outside, the Himalayas look very white, very beautiful. But once you enter, it is very harsh, cold, minus 40-5 degrees, freezing, very cold, not habitable. Similarly, Singha Durbar looks like that. From the outside, it looks like there are army and police, ministers are traveling in cars, MPs are speaking, how good the management must be inside. But Singha Durbar is so harsh, it doesn't see anything beyond its own area and its own perimeter, the ministers don't. I am not just saying this to the current government, this kind of practice has been developing since past governments. Therefore, I did not discuss anything in the budget. I wanted to raise a few points regarding my sector. One thing is that Sagarmatha is the highest mountain in the world. This year, 1,004 people climbed it. Many people were proud that 1,004 people climbed Sagarmatha. I am not proud of that. Sagarmatha is ruined now. Why is it ruined? Because we made Sagarmatha easy. We sold diamonds for the price of silver. Therefore, we must now sell Sagarmatha for the price of diamonds and maintain the value of Sagarmatha. Therefore, Honorable Minister, the royalty of Sagarmatha must be increased even more than this, one thing. The royalty of Sagarmatha. 93 If the Himalayas continue to be climbed like this, and if we keep climbing here and there, climbing the Himalayas is not like climbing a hill or going for a hike, we know what the environment there is like. Now, if the Ministry of Tourism cannot maintain the policies and regulations properly in such a situation, then in 20 years, the Himalayas, Sagarmatha, will not remain in good condition, and we will have to face the situation of being defamed in the world. I have drawn the attention of the ministry to this as well. Now, what is tourism like? Tourism, the minister spoke a lot about tourism. The tourism of the Himalayas was not even touched upon in the policies and programs. But we Nepalis do not have the mentality to eat the fruits that are already ripe. We look for other fruits. But if we manage the ripe fruits and look for some marketization, those ripe fruits will give us returns immediately. But if we start looking for other tourism, make a management plan for new tourism, do it, make a sustainable long-term plan. It will create a problem of what kind of future it will create. Therefore, the minister should think about this. Apart from Himalayan tourism, I don't think there is any other tourism for foreigners to come to Nepal. I hope you will pay attention to this. Another thing is that in the Himalayan region, the minister also spoke about Twin Otters. If there are Twin Otters, now these Twin Otters are small planes. If you do not provide concessions for them in Nepal, if you do not manage them, if you do not do it, then in 10 years, there will be no small planes left in Nepal, and no airport in the hilly region will be operational. Therefore, if you provide facilities and manage them in some way, only then will their existence remain, otherwise, no airline is in favor of operating Twin Otters, and all airlines in the Himalayan region of Nepal will not be operational with the current type of airports, it seems. I want to draw the minister's attention to that as well. Another thing is that the road management that we wanted to do, and the Sagarmatha region, now this year a title called tourism road has been brought into the budget. But if we expand 72 kilometers of road there, 72 kilometers of road from the district headquarters to above Lukla... If managed, it will be a revolutionary step in the tourism sector, and we can provide employment to 200,000 people. Therefore, I have drawn your attention to this as well. Why did I want to raise these points? Because I did not expect many things. Why didn't I expect them? Because the biggest thing is that you bring money into the system. Do not neglect the federal system. Maintain the federal system, the federal system will not be a burden to Singha Durbar. The people in the villages will develop. Therefore, my humble request is that efforts be made to advance the federal system without tampering with it. Thank you. Honorable Chairperson: Honorable Member Kiran Babu Shrestha, time 11 minutes. (1:59 PM) After this, Honorable Member Shri Krishna Prasad Adhikari. Honorable Mr. Kiran Babu Shrestha (Nepali Congress): Honorable Chairperson, (1:59 PM) I am going to present some of my views in this respected house on some allocation titles related to the budget for the fiscal year 2083/084, which the Honorable Finance Minister is going to present. I think this is an important opportunity to test how wisely, how transparently, how result-oriented, and how much in the public interest the tax money collected from the public is being spent. Money goes to the ministry, the budget is spent, but has the spent amount been able to bring positive change in the lives of the people? Can it? And I think this is the time to review the budget priorities, implementation, capacity, achievements, challenges, and expected results. The development of any nation is not measured solely by large buildings, wide roads, or high bridges. The real measure of development is determined by how capable, how educated, how healthy the citizens are, how prosperous the farmers are, how productive the industries are, and how much dignified employment the youth have found in their own country. Especially today, I seek permission to briefly present some of my views regarding some ministries, including the Ministry of Youth, Labor, and Employment, related to this. The greatest asset of any nation is its youth power. Youth are the energy, courage, change, and equality of the nation. If the state cannot invest in the youth of today, the foundation of the nation's future will be weak. Therefore, many developed countries have taken youth as capital, formulated policies accordingly, and moved forward on the path of development. Since the youth of the nation are strong pillars and foundations, there is no doubt that the country will move forward on the path of progress and prosperity only if the youth are guided in the right direction. Development is not possible without their intellect, wisdom, capability, skill, and participation. It is necessary to utilize their strength in nation-building and make them aware of their rights and dutiful. At the same time, the state must be capable of valuing their qualifications, skills, and capabilities appropriately and providing employment opportunities. Honorable Chairperson, unemployment causes poverty. Poverty causes unemployment. Income from agriculture is good. Nepal is plagued by the problem of unemployment. Due to lack of industrialization, lack of private sector business, and other reasons, the number of unemployed people is increasing every year. There are no employment opportunities in rural areas, and even in the limited employment in urban areas, due to not receiving adequate remuneration, it is difficult to make a daily living, forcing most of the country's youth to go for foreign employment and sweat it out on foreign soil. Not only that. They are forced to work in the 3D of English, i.e., Difficulty, Danger, and Dirty. Today, the fields in the villages are lying fallow. There is a shortage of skilled manpower in industries. Due to the lack of employment, the youth are forced to go abroad. Remittance has become a major source of the country's economy.

6. Millions of Nepali youth have earned a living by shedding sweat abroad, supporting the country's economy. Now we have to ask ourselves. Is our goal always to send youth abroad, or to create dignified employment within Nepal? Article 33(2) of the Constitution of Nepal states that every citizen shall have the right to choose employment. Similarly, Article 21(j) provides for policies related to employment to make foreign employment free from exploitation, safe, and organized, to guarantee and regulate the employment and rights of workers, and to encourage the investment of capital, skills, technology, and experience earned from foreign employment in productive sectors within the country. However, despite all these arrangements, the situation has not changed as expected in practice, neither yesterday nor today. Due to this, over time, disappointment gradually spread in the hopes of the youth, and dissatisfaction grew. In this state of dissatisfaction, we recently witnessed and experienced the revolt in the name of the "Jinjing" movement as a vivid example of how the youth power can be misused to fish in troubled waters. I believe we have learned a good lesson from this. Now the country has taken a new course. The majority of the leadership in the country is young. There is a majority government of one party. There are no obstacles to policy formulation and implementation. Now the current government has a golden opportunity to advance as the youth have envisioned. Such an opportunity does not come to everyone all the time. History is a witness that others also had such opportunities in the past, but we must admit that they lost that opportunity. I wish that the current government and the ruling leadership do not have to face a situation like that of the Iranian king Reza Pahlavi, who said, "I was in Iran yesterday, but I didn't know Iran. But today I am outside Iran, and I know Iran." And I also request that the youth do not feel that they have fallen into a trap after escaping the lake. She also points out a reduction in the education budget, particularly for teachers and community schools, despite the goal of a digital age. While acknowledging an increase in the budget for the Ministry of Women and Children, she argues it is still insufficient.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker discusses the inadequate support for youth employment and the lack of budget allocation for industries and businesses. They also highlight the reduction in budget for universities and former MPs, urging the government to reconsider these cuts. The speaker further points out the neglect of tourism promotion in remote areas and the dire situation of women and children in safe houses, emphasizing the need for basic education.

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Sonam Geljen Sherpa discusses the disconnect between the government's perspective in Singha Durbar and the realities of the Himalayas, using it as a metaphor for the government's limited understanding of ground realities. He criticizes the devaluation of Sagarmatha by making it too accessible and advocates for increasing its royalty to reflect its true value. He also raises concerns about the sustainability of Himalayan tourism and the management of small aircraft like Twin Otters, urging for better policies and infrastructure.

speakers.name: Sonam Geljen Sherpa
speakers.topic: Critique of government perspective, Sagarmatha's value, tourism, and infrastructure

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Kiran Babu Shrestha addresses the budget for FY 2083/084, emphasizing the need for transparency and effectiveness in public spending. He highlights the importance of youth as a national asset and criticizes the current situation of unemployment, leading to foreign labor migration. He stresses that national development should be measured by citizen well-being, education, health, and dignified employment opportunities within the country.

speakers.name: Kiran Babu Shrestha
speakers.topic: Budget review, youth empowerment, unemployment, and national development

sections.name: Main Business
sections.summary_en: The speaker discusses the issue of youth employment and foreign labor, highlighting constitutional provisions and the gap between policy and practice. They critique the budget allocation for the Ministry of Labor, Employment, and Social Security, questioning its sufficiency for various programs and noting a decrease from the previous year. The speaker also touches upon the challenges faced by returning migrants and the need for better support systems. The discussion then shifts to the Ministry of Education, with the speaker expressing concern over the declining share of the education budget and its impact on human capital development, while also pointing out unresolved issues in the education sector.

The speaker also discusses issues related to problematic cooperatives, the need for returning depositors' funds, and strengthening regulatory mechanisms. Finally, they touch upon the Ministry of Federal Affairs and General Administration, emphasizing the need for investment in local governance, digital services, and the implementation of the Federal Civil Service Act.

He also criticized the lack of transparency in the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation's budget and the absence of programs to support young scientists. He questioned the allocation of funds for vehicles and observatories while basic educational needs remain unmet.

sections.summary_en: Honorable Member Khamm Bahadur Khalti presented his views on the proposed budget for the Ministry of Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs and the Ministry of Land Management, Cooperatives, and Poverty Alleviation. He compared the programs and objectives of the current and previous fiscal years, noting similarities and some shifts in focus, particularly towards digitization and efficiency. He emphasized that budget success should be measured by citizen impact, not just expenditure.

sections.summary_en: The speaker discusses the government's approach to landless settlements, highlighting concerns about the eviction of people from hold centers and the provision of inadequate financial compensation. The speaker also criticizes delays and irregularities in land revenue and surveying, calls for result-oriented poverty alleviation programs, and demands stricter cooperative regulations. Additionally, the speaker raises concerns about the depletion of Guti property and urges the government to protect and manage it properly. The speaker criticizes the government for violating the constitution by abolishing trade unions and student organizations, interfering with the judiciary and legislature, and using ordinances to bypass parliament. The speaker also condemns the intimidation of constitutional officials and calls for the Prime Minister to be accountable.

She pointed out the absence of science in the policy and program documents and the concentration of funds at the federal level, neglecting provincial and local needs, and urged for increased budget and decentralized science programs.
